html:
SMTO-EML-0014 — Your email was stopped before it was sent

GUID: 5bb80ff5-6042-567e-bed5-3e9cf9453437
Slug: email-cancelled
Domain: EML · Subsystem: email-smtp

What happened

  • The email step was cancelled, for example because the task was stopped, before SMTO handed the message content to the mail server. The email was not sent.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. First, check the sender mailbox's Sent folder (if your provider keeps one), or ask a recipient, whether the email arrived. SMTO recorded that it stopped before handing the message over, and a quick check confirms no copy went out before you send it again.
  2. If you still want it sent, ask SMTO in the conversation to send the email again and approve it when asked. SMTO never repeats a stopped email on its own.
  3. If you didn't select Stop yourself, check in Settings › Setup › Gateways whether the Gateway was being updated at that time. Updating a Gateway stops the tasks running on it, which cancels an email in progress.

What success looks like

  • SMTO reports the mail server accepted the message, and it arrives only once.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't send the email several times in a row to be sure; check that it hasn't arrived first.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The SMTP operation was cancelled (IOCancelled) before message content transmission began, and the outcome was recorded as failed_before_send at the last confirmed stage.

What this means

  • SMTP I/O raises IOCancelled outside an unresolved body-transmission phase and records the cancelled outcome at its confirmed stage. Only correlated SMTP stage and receipt evidence establish acceptance. An accepted message cannot be recalled by cancellation, and unknown delivery blocks automatic resend; diagnostic rendering sends no email.

Why this can happen

  • SMTP I/O raises IOCancelled outside an unresolved body-transmission phase and records the cancelled outcome at its confirmed stage.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect delivery receipt and last_confirmed_stage; interruption during uncertain transmission is classified separately as unknown effect.

How to fix it

  • Confirm last_confirmed_stage precedes MESSAGE_BYTES_TRANSMITTING and status is failed_before_send, then start a new, separately approved send if still wanted. Cancellation cannot undo a server-accepted message, so check delivery evidence before sending again.
  • Inspect delivery evidence before starting another operation. Cancellation cannot undo a server-accepted message.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the reported condition and check delivery evidence before starting another operation.

How to verify the fix

  • Original delivery evidence is reconciled before any new send, with accepted messages never treated as undone.

What not to do

  • Do not expose passwords, access tokens, authorization codes or SMTP authentication payloads.
  • Do not automatically repeat an operation whose remote effect is unknown.

Technical notes

  • Only correlated SMTP stage and receipt evidence establish acceptance. An accepted message cannot be recalled by cancellation, and unknown delivery blocks automatic resend; diagnostic rendering sends no email.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
